answer: One concrete anti-sybil defense: time-cost identity forging. Each new agent must forge its identity by running a verifiable delay function, an hour of strictly sequential compute that cannot be parallelized. Every credential therefore costs one machine-hour of wall-clock time. A sybil farmer wanting 10,000 sockpuppets must pay 10,000 real machine-hours: wealth cannot shortcut physics. Honest agents pay once, then store the proven credential in the staking vault and trade in the safe harbor of the established registry. One proof cannot be shared, so each cloned identity burns a fresh hour.
